name: VPS Configuration help
description: The gate plugin's Help mode entries (help@1).
author: Brett

entries.title: VPS Configuration
entries.text: How the VPS runs builds (this screen was named Gate & rules): the rules a PR must pass before it lands, the build rules, the auto-lander that lands it, and the history of every change. Same calls as `axf gate …`, the gate_* and lander_* MCP tools and voice (“open VPS Configuration”).

entries.title: VPS Configuration settings
entries.text: This plugin's settings under Settings → Plugins: how often the open tab refreshes, how much History keeps, and which tab it opens on.

entries.title: VPS Configuration settings
entries.text: This plugin's settings under Settings → Plugins: how often the open tab refreshes, how much History keeps, and which tab it opens on.

entries.title: Rules
entries.text: Every gate rule with its on/off switch, severity and settings.

entries.title: Auto-lander
entries.text: The Merge queue switch, the lander's status, the PRs waiting to land and its last runs.

entries.title: History
entries.text: Every rule change and lander action: who, when, before and after.

entries.title: Rule
entries.text: The rule's name; with two lines a row, what it checks underneath. Tap the row to open its settings.

entries.title: Checks
entries.text: What the rule looks at: CI, tests, theme, controls, UI Review, a clash with main, or a policy.

entries.title: Severity
entries.text: Block: the PR waits until it passes. Warn: it lands and History notes it. Info: only recorded.

entries.title: Run by
entries.text: Who evaluates the rule: the console now, axf-molly once that container owns the gate. A rule is never run by both.

entries.title: On
entries.text: Switches the rule on or off at once. Off rules are skipped for every PR.

entries.title: PR
entries.text: The pull request number to check, for example 705.

entries.title: Check a PR
entries.text: Shows whether that PR can land, rule by rule, from what the lander knows. It changes nothing.

entries.title: Reset to defaults
entries.text: Puts every gate rule back to its default. It asks first; History keeps what was there.

entries.title: Save
entries.text: Saves the changed fields. The change is written to History. On Approval rules it sends the draft to axHub from this browser on Brett's own hub session, and only Brett's own click does it.

entries.title: Merge queue
entries.text: On: ready PRs go through the stacked merge queue and the one-at-a-time lander is off. Off (the default): the auto-lander lands each finished build one at a time, main merged in first. Takes effect at once.

entries.title: Land now
entries.text: Puts the selected PR at the head of the line in the current mode. It asks first and still has to pass every rule; nothing is merged directly.

entries.title: Land next
entries.text: Puts this PR at the head of the line. It asks first and still has to pass every rule.

entries.title: Why pause
entries.text: Optional: why you pause the lander. It shows on the status card, in History and in the alert.

entries.title: Pause
entries.text: Stops the lander from starting anything new; what is landing now finishes. Resume carries on.

entries.title: Resume
entries.text: Starts the lander again in its current mode.

entries.title: Show
entries.text: Which History entries to list: all, rule changes, or lander actions.

entries.title: Held by
entries.text: The gate rule that keeps this PR from landing.

entries.title: Why
entries.text: Why the PR waits, in plain words.

entries.title: Result
entries.text: How the run ended: landed, landing, idle, skipped or error.

entries.title: Refresh every (seconds)
entries.text: How often the open VPS Configuration tab asks the lander again (5 to 600).

entries.title: History size (entries kept)
entries.text: How many History entries are kept; the oldest go first (50 to 20000).

entries.title: Tab it opens on
entries.text: The tab VPS Configuration opens on, unless you were on another one last time.

entries.title: Show the lists as
entries.text: How the gate's lists are drawn: a grid with two lines a row, cards (best on a phone), or a compact one-line grid. Unset, it follows the skin.

entries.title: Build rules
entries.text: Every rule a build has to follow, in one list: who does it (the VPS or the build session), when, its check and fixer, on or off, and how it went last time. VPS rules are done by the VPS and never reach a session's brief, so nothing is done twice. Same as `axf gate build-rules …`, the gate_build_rules_* MCP tools and voice (gate.build-rules.*).

entries.title: Build rules tab
entries.text: Open it with console_show view:gate/tab:gate.tabs=build-rules or the voice action gate.build-rules.open. A rule's History opens with gate.build-rules.open:<rule>.

entries.title: The rule
entries.text: The words a build session reads in its brief, or what the VPS enforces. Keep it to what has to happen.

entries.title: Who does it
entries.text: The VPS: it is run by the dispatcher, the end hook or the gate, with its check and fixer, and never reaches a brief. The build session: it goes into the brief block you pick.

entries.title: When
entries.text: When the VPS acts on it: before launch, in the brief, after the build, or at the gate before the PR lands.

entries.title: Fixer
entries.text: What the VPS runs when the check fails (for example home-card writes the missing Home card); then it checks again. None = the failure blocks and shows in History.

entries.title: Brief block
entries.text: Where a session rule goes in the brief: the Look, API or Checkpoints line, or the Rules for this job list.

entries.title: Goes to
entries.text: Build sessions only, sessions with Brett only, or both.

entries.title: Only when the build mentions
entries.text: Comma-separated words. The rule goes into a build's brief only when its title or text names one of them; empty = every build.

entries.title: Who
entries.text: Show the rules the VPS does, the ones the session does, or all of them.

entries.title: Phase
entries.text: Which rules to run for the build: before launch, after the build, or at the gate.

entries.title: Dry run
entries.text: Checks the build's rules and says what the fixers would write, without changing anything.

entries.title: Run now
entries.text: Runs the build's rules now: checks, fixes what fails in the build's worktree (committed on its branch), checks again, and writes it all to History.

entries.title: Add a rule
entries.text: Opens the rule dialog for a new build rule.

entries.title: Last result
entries.text: How the rule went the last time the VPS ran it: pass, fixed, fail or skipped (its checker runs elsewhere).

entries.title: axf gate build-rules
entries.text: The CLI: list, get, add, edit, on, off, delete (two-step), history, runs, run <build> --phase before|after|gate [--dry-run], brief <build>. Also node apps/console-web/plugins/gate/build-rules.mjs.

entries.title: Build cap
entries.text: How many builds the VPS runs at once: Builds at once, the emergency slots and the orchestrator's steps in parallel side by side, with what runs now. A note says so when the numbers disagree. Same values as `axf gate build-cap`, the vps_build_cap MCP tools and “what is the build cap”.

entries.title: Build cap
entries.text: The hard cap and the emergency slots are the host's limit (only Brett changes them, from his own signed-in console). Steps in parallel is the orchestrator's setting and can be changed from anywhere. The smaller of hard cap and steps in parallel is what really runs at once.

entries.title: Builds at once
entries.text: The most builds the VPS ever runs at once (1 to 64). The same setting as Settings → Plugins → Agent cap → Builds at once: one stored key. Sessions, MCP and voice can read it; only Brett's signed-in console can change it.

entries.title: Emergency slots
entries.text: Extra places only an emergency build may take, counted apart from Builds at once (0 to 8, 0 = off). Only Brett's signed-in console can change it.

entries.title: Steps in parallel
entries.text: How many steps of one build the orchestrator sends at once (1 to 12). Above Builds at once it changes nothing: only that many run.

entries.title: Refresh
entries.text: Reads the numbers again now. The tab also refreshes by itself.

entries.title: Undo edits
entries.text: Puts the fields back to the saved values. Nothing is saved.

entries.title: axf gate build-cap
entries.text: `axf gate build-cap` shows the three numbers and the note; `axf gate build-cap set stepsInParallel 4` changes steps in parallel. The hard cap and emergency slots are not settable from the CLI.

entries.title: Approval rules
entries.text: The rules axHub uses to decide each call: which tools run at once, which hold on the veto countdown and for how long, which wait for Brett's confirm and which never run. Same rules as `axf gate approvals`, the vps_approval_rules MCP tools and “what are the approval rules”.

entries.title: Approval rules
entries.text: Each service has an ordered list of rules. A rule names tools (one name, or a pattern where * is anything, like build_* or *), a decision and a hold length. The first rule that matches a tool decides it; a tool with its own entry ignores the rules until Let the rules decide clears it. Edits are a draft: nothing changes on axHub until Brett presses Save.

entries.title: Apply the default
entries.text: Sets Brett's rule in one go: only shell commands on the VPS hold on the veto countdown (vps run and launch, the console terminal run, Vinny command run). Everything else in the console and the orchestrator runs at once, model upgrades keep their confirm and deletes keep their approval. It takes Brett's own click: a session, MCP, the CLI and voice cannot press it. The tab asks first; Yes, apply the default is the press that does it.

entries.title: Yes, apply the default
entries.text: The answer to the question Apply the default asked. This press sets the default on axHub. It works from the phone app too: the question is on the page, not a pop-up.

entries.title: Yes, save
entries.text: The answer to the question Save asked. This press sends the draft to axHub. If it can't be saved, the reason shows on the tab and the draft is kept.

entries.title: Sign in to axHub
entries.text: Shows when this page is not on Brett's axHub sign-in, or when the sign-in ran out during a save. It opens axHub's sign-in and comes back to this tab; the draft waits. Then press Save or Apply the default again.

entries.title: Discard draft
entries.text: Drops every staged edit. axHub was never changed, so nothing is undone there.

entries.title: Let the rules decide
entries.text: A tool with an entry of its own ignores every rule. On: Save clears those entries for this service so the rules decide. Denied tools and deletes keep theirs.

entries.title: Update rule
entries.text: Puts the edited tools pattern and hold length for this rule into the draft. Nothing changes on axHub until Save.

entries.title: Move rule up
entries.text: Moves the rule one place up. Order matters: the first rule that matches a tool decides it.

entries.title: Move rule down
entries.text: Moves the rule one place down. A rule under a catch-all (*) decides nothing.

entries.title: Remove rule
entries.text: Takes the rule out of the draft. The tools it decided fall to the next matching rule, or to the service.

entries.title: Add rule
entries.text: Adds the new rule to this service's draft, above a closing catch-all (*) so it can still decide something.

entries.title: axf gate approvals
entries.text: `axf gate approvals` shows the rules. `axf gate approvals add vps run veto 60`, `edit vps 1 vetoSeconds 30`, `remove vps 2`, `move vps 3 1`, `clear-own axf-console`, `default` and `discard` stage edits in the draft. Nothing is saved from the CLI: Brett saves from his console.

entries.title: Passes
entries.text: The one home for passes: veto passes (start one, approve or deny a request, revoke, undo, the longest pass), the hub's timed passes and the Go pass. Same calls as the pass MCP tools, `axf pass …` and “start a pass for 30 minutes”.

entries.title: Passes
entries.text: A veto pass lets commands run without the veto countdown for a while. Pick a scope and the minutes (never more than the longest pass), start it, and revoke or undo it from the list. Passes moved here from Token control and from the axHub passes pages.

entries.title: Veto passes
entries.text: Start a pass, see what is on and waiting per scope, approve, deny, revoke or undo, and set the longest pass.

entries.title: axHub passes
entries.text: The hub's timed passes: what each covers, time left, extend, revoke, and the calls that ran under it.

entries.title: Go pass
entries.text: One pass for a whole Claude session that can't reach axHub: go for some hours, or end it now.

entries.title: Scope
entries.text: What the pass covers. Everything is every command on every plugin; a narrower scope covers only token changes there.

entries.title: Minutes
entries.text: How long the pass lasts, from 1 to the longest pass. A longer number is cut to the longest pass.

entries.title: Reason
entries.text: Optional: why the pass is needed. It is kept with the pass.

entries.title: Include irreversible deletes
entries.text: Hard deletes nothing can bring back also skip the confirm while this pass is on. Off, they still confirm.

entries.title: Start pass
entries.text: Starts the pass for the scope and minutes picked. From Brett's signed-in console it is on at once; anyone else files a request he approves.

entries.title: Approve
entries.text: Turns a waiting request into a pass.

entries.title: Deny
entries.text: Refuses a waiting request. Nothing changes.

entries.title: Undo
entries.text: Puts back every change made under this pass in one go, and says what could not be rolled back.

entries.title: Revoke
entries.text: Ends the pass now. Calls go back to the veto countdown.

entries.title: Longest pass
entries.text: How long a veto pass may last at most (1 to 240 minutes). A longer request is cut to this.

entries.title: Time zone
entries.text: The time zone the plain answers use (“until 10:42 AM”), for example America/New_York.

entries.title: Note
entries.text: Optional: what the pass is for. Shown in the pass.

entries.title: Go
entries.text: Starts the pass for the hours you picked. Sessions without the hub may work until it ends.

entries.title: Ran under a pass
entries.text: Opens the approvals log filtered to every call that ran under a pass instead of waiting on the veto countdown.

entries.title: Extend
entries.text: Keeps the pass on for that many minutes from now. The calls it covers keep running at once until the new end.

entries.title: Its calls
entries.text: Opens the approvals log filtered to the calls that ran under this pass.

entries.title: Service
entries.text: Which service the pass covers, for example axf-console. Only calls from that service run under it.

entries.title: Scope
entries.text: The control@1 targets the pass covers, comma separated; * matches anything, so tokens.* covers every token. Leave it empty when you list tools instead.

entries.title: Tools
entries.text: The tools the pass covers, comma separated. Empty means every tool inside the scope. Destructive tools never run under a pass.

entries.title: Server auto-lander
entries.text: The VPS fixes and lands finished builds by itself, every minute: merges main into a clash, starts a fix session for red CI, sends green PRs to the merge queue. After 3 failed tries of one kind it stops and puts a red item in the systems check with Fix.

entries.title: Fix
entries.text: Resets the selected build's attempts and starts a fix session for it on the next tick, whatever CI says.

entries.title: Retry
entries.text: Resets the selected build's attempts and escalation; the next tick tries again from attempt 1.

entries.title: axf gate auto-lander
entries.text: status, show <build>, run [--now], retry <build>, fix <build>, pause, resume, settings, set <key> <value>. Same as REST /api/plugins/gate/auto-lander and MCP gate_auto_lander_*.

entries.title: Fix and land by itself
entries.text: On: the server auto-lander merges main in, starts fix sessions and lands builds by itself every minute. Off: it still reads every build but changes nothing.

entries.title: Push to my phone when it gives up
entries.text: One phone push per build the auto-lander gives up on (after the set number of failed tries). The systems check banner item shows either way.

entries.title: Land by itself
entries.text: Turns “Land by itself” on or off. It takes effect straight away and is remembered. Part of VPS Configuration.

steps.say: Rules: what every PR must pass before it lands. Switch a rule off or change its severity here.
Auto-lander: Server is the VPS auto-lander that fixes and lands builds by itself; Merge line is the Merge queue switch and what waits.
History: every change and lander action, with before and after.
